## Tours through Areguá: what the program includes

[Areguá](/paraguay/place/aregua/) lies near [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) on Lake Ypacaraí. The town is known for pottery, workshops and craft shops. Unlike the capital, where itineraries often focus on historic buildings and museums, the main experiences here are local artisans' products, small streets and lake views.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} following a main route through Areguá. **A visit to the town does not mean a separate multi-day stay in Areguá**: check the activities planned for the particular day and the neighboring stops.

On the [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), Areguá is scheduled for day eleven. Travelers leave Asunción, discover the crafts town, then head to [San Bernardino](/paraguay/place/san-bernardino/) and continue toward the hills and natural areas of Guairá. This sequence introduces several different parts of eastern Paraguay in a single day.

## What makes Areguá interesting

The town is famous for producing pottery. Artisans make vessels, decorative figures and everyday objects; their work can be found in markets and workshops. Areguá's pottery tradition is recognized as part of Paraguay's intangible cultural heritage. For travelers, the stop offers an opportunity to see handmade work in a place where craftsmanship remains a living occupation.

Another feature is the town's position on hills beside Lake Ypacaraí. Streets with houses and small shops lead to places with views over the water. The lake gives Areguá a distinctive setting, but visiting the town does not automatically include swimming, a boat trip or a particular gallery: such activities must be explicitly stated in the itinerary.

Travelers especially interested in crafts should decide whether a general stop is sufficient or whether they want a dedicated workshop visit. The published tour mentions the town and craft shops; a pottery class, purchases and a personal meeting with a particular artist are not guaranteed services.

## Combining Areguá with San Bernardino and Guairá

Areguá fits naturally into a route from Asunción toward the lakeside areas. In [San Bernardino](/paraguay/place/san-bernardino/), attention shifts to the lake and relaxation amid greenery. The itinerary then continues into the natural regions of Guairá, with hills, forests and waterfalls.

These are not three identical stops. Areguá is best for craft culture, San Bernardino for lakeside scenery and Guairá for discovering a hillier part of the country. Combining culture and nature is what justifies the longer excursion beyond the capital.

| Stop | Main appeal |
|---|---|
| Areguá | Pottery and crafts |
| San Bernardino | Lake and walks |
| Guairá | Hills and nature |
| Asunción | Historic center |

If one stop is especially important, read the day's description rather than estimating visit length from a list of place names. On a multi-day journey, travel between places can take most of the time outside a city.

## Areguá within a longer two-country journey

The [16-day tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) starts in Uruguay, where travelers visit Montevideo, Colonia del Sacramento, Canelones and Punta del Este. It then continues through Paraguay: the capital, the [Chaco region](/paraguay/place/chaco/), crafts-focused Areguá and other areas. The final section includes [Ciudad del Este](/paraguay/place/ciudad-del-este/) and Iguazu Falls.

This tour is suitable for those seeking a broad view of South America: Uruguay's wine regions and ocean coast alongside Paraguay's urban culture and dry landscapes. If your only aim is Areguá pottery, a much longer international itinerary may be unnecessary.

For other programs within one country, see the [Paraguay tours catalog](/paraguay/tour/). Not every route passing through Asunción includes Areguá: sharing a starting city does not establish a visit to the crafts center.

## Planning the visit: timing and season

A short stop in a crafts town needs free time for walking and purchases. If you want to see a potter at work, confirm in advance whether a workshop visit is part of the itinerary and whether it will be open on the selected day. Individual shop opening hours may change.

Paraguay has hot Southern Hemisphere summers and milder winters. Sun and temperature are especially important for walking around town, and rain protection is useful in wet weather. An international journey also requires coordination of flights, currencies and documents for every country visited; requirements depend on nationality and route.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Areguá

### Is Areguá a compulsory stop on the 16-day tour?

Yes. The town is part of the main route on the [Uruguay and Paraguay journey](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) and appears on day eleven.

### Can visitors see pottery made by local artisans?

Yes. Handcrafted pottery is one of the main reasons to visit Areguá. However, a particular class or a visit to a specific workshop must be confirmed in the conditions for that excursion day.

### Is there an overnight stay in Areguá itself?

The published program treats Areguá as a stop while traveling from Asunción through other regions. No separate overnight stay in the town is advertised.

### How does this differ from an ordinary Asunción city tour?

[Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) offers an introduction to the capital's history and museums, while Areguá showcases crafts and the lakeside part of the country. The full multi-day itinerary combines both.

## Asunción: what to see in Paraguay's capital in 1–2 days

**Asunción** is the capital of [Paraguay](/paraguay/) on the Paraguay River. Founded in the sixteenth century, the city retains historic districts, public squares, museums, churches and a waterfront overlooking the river valley. The country's independence story is easier to understand here than from a single sightseeing stop: many monuments lie within a relatively compact city center.

One busy day is enough for a first introduction; another is useful if you want to visit museums, markets and newer districts without rushing.

## Independence House and the historic center

One of the principal places to explore national history is the **Independence House (Casa de la Independencia)**. Built in the eighteenth century, this colonial house is associated with preparations for the events of May 1811, when Paraguay began to achieve independence from the Spanish crown.

From here, you can follow central streets toward the **National Pantheon of Heroes** and public squares. The Pantheon serves as a national memorial, while nearby buildings reveal a mixture of colonial and later architectural styles.

Other recognizable landmarks include **López Palace**, administrative buildings near the river, the old Cabildo and historic churches. It is easier to explore them on a continuous walking route than through several short drives between neighboring streets.

## Costanera waterfront and the Paraguay River

**Costanera** is Asunción's waterfront promenade, designed for walking and relaxing beside the water. It offers views of the bay and opposite bank. In the late afternoon, it is a pleasant place to pause after the museums and streets of the center.

The city stands on the **Paraguay River**, not the Paraná: the rivers join farther south. This is an important geographical distinction, especially when planning journeys to other parts of the country.

In hot weather, a waterfront walk is more comfortable outside the sunniest hours. River weather, seasonal rains and water levels can affect conditions along individual stretches of the shore.

## Loma San Jerónimo and city markets

**Loma San Jerónimo** is known for colorful houses, narrow passageways and local cultural initiatives. The neighborhood has its own history, with daily life as interesting as the facades.

Markets and shopping districts offer crafts, textiles and food products. One distinctive national art tradition is the delicate lace known as **ñandutí**. When buying it, ask where it was made and whether it is handmade, since an ordinary retail stall does not establish the provenance of every item.

Asunción offers a good introduction to how Spanish and Guaraní coexist in the urban environment. Many signs and everyday expressions reflect Paraguay's bilingual culture.

## What to try: tereré, mate and local food

**Tereré**, a cold infusion of yerba mate often prepared with herbs, and hot mate are widely consumed in Paraguay. Tereré is especially visible in daily life in the hot climate: people often carry a thermos and drinking vessel.

Local food includes **sopa paraguaya**, a baked corn-based dish, and **chipa**, traditional baked goods made with cassava starch and cheese. To discover the cuisine, choose a café or restaurant where these dishes are actually served rather than assuming they appear on every menu.

If food culture matters as much as museums, allow time for a proper meal instead of trying to squeeze every experience into a brief transit stop.

## Planning 1 or 2 days

| Time | Main experiences |
|---|---|
| Half a day | Center and Pantheon |
| 1 day | Museums, center, Costanera |
| 2 days | Markets, neighborhoods, food |

For a general introduction, choose the [Asunción city tour](/paraguay/asuncion/asuncion-city-tour/). A separate second day allows time for museum collections and districts beyond the historical core.

From the capital, you can continue exploring [other places in Paraguay](/paraguay/place/), including crafts towns and natural regions. When planning a longer journey, compare [Paraguay tours](/paraguay/tour/) by their actual itineraries and travel time.

## Climate, transport and practical details

Asunción can be hot and humid; during Southern Hemisphere summer, morning and late-afternoon walks are especially comfortable. Sudden thunderstorms and strong sun call for flexible scheduling. Check current local arrangements for public transport and taxis; not all city journeys are practical on foot.

The Paraguayan guaraní is the national currency, while Spanish and Guaraní are both official languages. For purchases at smaller establishments, plan for local currency and do not assume every foreign bank card will work everywhere.

## Frequently asked questions about Asunción

### Which river is Asunción on?

The Paraguay River, beside a broad river bay. The Costanera waterfront lets visitors see it directly.

### How many days should I spend in Asunción?

One day works for the main central monuments and an evening walk. Two days provide more time for museums, markets and food.

### What should I see first?

Independence House, the National Pantheon of Heroes, historic streets and Costanera.

### What is tereré known for?

It is a popular Paraguayan cold drink made with yerba mate, often with herbs, enjoyed throughout the day.

### Is Asunción a good starting point for a journey across the country?

Yes. The capital is a convenient place to plan onward travel, though journey times depend on the chosen towns and roads.

## Tours through Asunción: which itinerary to choose

[Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) is Paraguay's capital on the Paraguay River. It offers an introduction to the country before visitors head to other regions: the dry forests of the Chaco, Jesuit missions, smaller towns and borderlands. The city itself preserves buildings from different historical periods, markets, museums and districts of modern urban life.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Asunción on their main route. **The first question is how many days you want to spend in the capital and where you will travel next.** On one tour, Asunción is a base for onward excursions; on another, it is just part of an international journey.

We offer two programs with different purposes:

| Format | Main focus |
|---|---|
| 8 days in Paraguay | Capital, Chaco, missions |
| 16 days in South America | Uruguay, Paraguay, Iguazu |

The [8-day Paraguay itinerary](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) starts in Asunción and travels through the [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/), Mennonite colonies and Jesuit heritage sites toward the country's southeast. The [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) connects both countries, adding nature, winemaking regions and Iguazu to the city tours. These involve significantly different allocations of time and transfers.

## If you want to discover Paraguay in depth

The [8-day program](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) begins with a sightseeing tour of Asunción. It names Independence House, the cathedral, National Pantheon of Heroes and Mercado Pettirossi. The itinerary then heads into the Chaco, where travelers visit [Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/) and learn about Mennonite colonies and the history of the Chaco War.

Later, the program continues to the Jesuit missions, southern parts of the country, [Ciudad del Este](/paraguay/place/ciudad-del-este/) and Itaipu. It is a choice for travelers who want a deeper understanding of Paraguay's history and geography rather than dividing a holiday between several countries.

The published program's name contains an earlier year. This alone does not confirm dates of future departures: the calendar, accommodation conditions and availability of individual visits must be checked for the specific journey. The main itinerary and its sights still make it possible to understand the purpose of the trip.

## If you want to combine Asunción with Uruguay and Iguazu

The [16-day tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) first explores Montevideo, Colonia del Sacramento, Canelones and Punta del Este. Paraguay follows. In Asunción, the program includes the historic center, López Palace, National Pantheon of Heroes, Independence House and Museo del Barro.

After the capital, travelers head into the [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/) and toward [Laguna Capitán](/paraguay/place/laguna-capitan/), then visit [Areguá](/paraguay/place/aregua/), [San Bernardino](/paraguay/place/san-bernardino/) and other areas. Toward the end, the route passes through [Ciudad del Este](/paraguay/place/ciudad-del-este/) and Iguazu Falls.

This option suits travelers seeking contrasts: Uruguay's ocean coast and vineyards, Paraguay's capital and crafts, Chaco landscapes and the famous waterfalls. But seeing so many regions necessarily involves transfers. If you want several relaxed days exclusively in Asunción, check how much time remains in the city within the international program.

## Choosing excursions in Asunción

The capital's best-known historic stops are the National Pantheon of Heroes, Independence House, López Palace and the cathedral. They relate to the colonial period, Paraguay's independence and the history of the republic. **What a sightseeing excursion includes is determined by its specific program, not the generic term “city tour.”**

Museo del Barro has a special place in the city's cultural life, presenting folk and contemporary art. On one trip you may prefer a museum-focused day; on another, old streets and markets. When time is short, decide on your priorities beforehand: architecture, history, art or everyday city life.

To expand the cultural program, consider a trip to [Areguá](/paraguay/place/aregua/), known for its pottery. It is included in the 16-day itinerary but is not among the compulsory stops on the 8-day tour. Tours passing through Asunción should therefore not be assumed to have identical suburban excursions.

## Asunción as a transport base

The capital is convenient for starting and finishing journeys across the country. However, a program that includes the Chaco, southern missions and border towns requires substantial travel by road. The stated tour duration includes transfers, accommodation changes and other journeys between regions.

A multi-country tour adds flights, border formalities and different currencies. Entry requirements depend on nationality, transit points and dates, so they cannot be summed up in one phrase for every visitor. The conditions of the chosen tour take priority over generic promises of universal assistance.

If you want Asunción to be the central destination of your trip, choose a route with enough hours in the city itself. If your main interest is South American geography, compare the full [Paraguay tours catalog](/paraguay/tour/) and the length of excursions beyond the capital.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Asunción

### Is Asunción included in both programs?

Yes. The city is on the main route of both the [8-day Paraguay tour](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) and the [16-day program including Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/). The number of days and additional stops differ.

### Do the tours include a trip to the Chaco?

Yes. Both programs include the [Chaco region](/paraguay/place/chaco/), though duration, order of visits and sites differ.

### Do all Asunción tours include Areguá?

No. [Areguá](/paraguay/place/aregua/) is part of the published 16-day itinerary but not on the 8-day tour's main list of places.

### Can I choose a tour of the capital alone?

This page's catalog covers multi-day tours through Asunción. For a standalone walk without a larger itinerary, browse the confirmed [Paraguay excursions](/paraguay/excursion/) and the precise conditions of an independent excursion.

### Which season is best for the journey?

Paraguay's Southern Hemisphere summers are hotter, while winters are generally milder. When choosing dates, consider not only Asunción but also conditions in the Chaco and other areas of the route: travel through several regions requires broader planning.

## Caapucú: Casa-Oratorio Cabañas and Paraguay's colonial history

Caapucú lies in the Paraguarí department, south of [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/). For travelers, it is a cultural stop along the road to the country's southern historic centers. The principal local attraction is **Casa-Oratorio Cabañas museum**, an old estate also known as Óga Guasu de los Cabañas and Alquería del Yaguary.

Here you can see a colonial-era residence and artifacts that tell the story of a family, religious life and the region's political events. Caapucú fits into an itinerary between the capital and southern towns, with separate time devoted to the historic museum.

## What is Casa-Oratorio Cabañas?

The name Casa-Oratorio combines two functions of the old building: **a home and a domestic prayer room**. According to Paraguay's National Secretariat of Culture, the complex dates back to the end of the seventeenth century. It is a type of rural estate in which family, farming and religious traditions were closely connected.

The house's history is linked to the Cabañas family. In **1724**, clashes took place here during the Comuneros movement. Later, the estate witnessed the period of the struggle for independence, political changes and the consequences of the great nineteenth-century war. This explains why the museum matters for more than its architecture: a single place offers a perspective on several periods of Paraguayan history.

In **1973**, the complex was transferred to the state on the condition that it be preserved as a museum. Extensive restoration began in **1992**. Today's exhibition therefore occupies a historic building whose present condition reflects many years of conservation work on the architecture and collection.

## What to see in the Cabañas museum

The permanent collection contains **wooden sculptures in the Jesuit tradition**, old church furnishings, silver objects from the oratory, chests, ceramic vessels and furniture. Documents reveal the estate's owners and everyday life in the region.

The collection brings several themes together. Religious images introduce Catholic practices in colonial society. Everyday objects show how the estate and household operated. Historical documents link the family's private life to events of national importance.

The National Secretariat of Culture identifies **Manuel Atanasio Cabañas** among the best-known historical figures associated with the site; he took part in the battles of Paraguarí and Tacuarí. His story adds a chapter about Paraguay's early independence to that of the building itself.

While visiting, pay attention to the building as well as the exhibits: its old walls, rooms and the arrangement of museum objects within the former estate. This is a different experience from seeing a collection in a modern purpose-built museum.

## Caapucú and the southern Jesuit missions

On our published [classic Paraguay itinerary](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/), Caapucú lies between [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) and [San Ignacio Guazú](/paraguay/place/san-ignacio-guazu/). The journey then continues to [Encarnación and Trinidad](/paraguay/place/encarnacion-and-trinidad/), where the theme of colonial history takes on a broader scale.

This sequence allows travelers to compare a **rural estate and private oratory** with churches and historic sites linked to the country's Jesuit heritage. In Caapucú, visitors discover one family's life and its domestic religious space; farther south, they encounter the history of settlements and community religious buildings.

The sites should not be confused: Casa-Oratorio Cabañas is not one of the large Jesuit missions. Its collection includes sculptures in the Jesuit tradition, but the museum stands apart from the historic complexes of southern Paraguay.

Our route title contains the year 2023, so it cannot be treated as confirmation of a future departure. For a different program, see our [Paraguay tours catalog](/paraguay/tour/), comparing the places visited and travel conditions.

## Planning a visit to Casa-Oratorio Cabañas

The museum is located on Ruta 1 Mariscal López in the Caapucú area. The state National Secretariat of Culture publishes visiting hours and access information, but check these before departure: opening can change during restoration, public holidays or special events.

To gain a deeper understanding of Paraguayan history, it is useful to arrange a guide familiar with the colonial estate, the Comuneros movement and the collection of religious objects. Do not assume that a Russian-language tour will necessarily be available on site.

Allow enough time on a journey south for both the drive and a proper look at the collection. A visit to the museum can become a substantial historical stop rather than a quick photograph of its façade.

## Frequently asked questions about Caapucú

### Where is Caapucú?

In the Paraguarí department, south of [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/), on the road toward Paraguay's southern historic regions.

### What is Casa-Oratorio Cabañas known for?

Its historic residence and domestic oratory dating from the late seventeenth century. The museum displays old sculptures, colonial household objects and documents.

### Is the Cabañas museum a Jesuit mission?

No. It is an old estate museum with religious objects. [San Ignacio Guazú](/paraguay/place/san-ignacio-guazu/) and the southern missions are different stops.

### Can Caapucú be visited on a journey from Asunción?

Yes. The museum is listed between the capital and the southern cultural centers on the [published southern Paraguay itinerary](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/). Check actual opening arrangements for the travel date.

## Tours through Caapucú: a historical stop on the way to the missions

[Caapucú](/paraguay/place/caapucu/) lies on the southbound route from [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/). It is a small but rewarding stop for travelers wanting to see Paraguay's colonial heritage beyond the capital. Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Caapucú on the main itinerary.

On the [8-day Paraguay journey](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/), Caapucú is visited on day five. Travelers leave Asunción in the morning, explore the Casa-Oratorio Cabañas museum, then continue to [San Ignacio Guazú](/paraguay/place/san-ignacio-guazu/) and arrive in [Encarnación](/paraguay/place/encarnacion-and-trinidad/) in the evening. This is **a stop within a continuous road journey**, not a separate multi-day tour with accommodation in Caapucú.

## Why Caapucú is worth a stop

The main visit is Casa-Oratorio Cabañas museum, also known as Oga Guasu de los Cabañas. It occupies a historic building dating from the end of the seventeenth century. Its collection includes colonial household objects, furniture, wooden religious sculptures and silver objects from the old oratory. Historical documents have also been preserved.

This is a good place to start learning about the lives of landowning families and communities in the colonial period. At subsequent stops, the story broadens: in [San Ignacio Guazú](/paraguay/place/san-ignacio-guazu/), travelers visit museum collections connected to the Jesuits, while farther on, near [Trinidad and Encarnación](/paraguay/place/encarnacion-and-trinidad/), archaeological remains of Jesuit settlements await.

The museum has its own opening and visiting rules. Before setting off, check the day of the week and actual exhibition access; the town appearing on the route does not guarantee that the museum will be open at any hour.

## How the day with Caapucú unfolds

Day five consists of three main stages:

1. **[Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/).** Departure from the capital after the previous days exploring the city and the Chaco region.
2. **[Caapucú](/paraguay/place/caapucu/).** A visit to Casa-Oratorio Cabañas, with colonial artifacts and regional history.
3. **[San Ignacio Guazú](/paraguay/place/san-ignacio-guazu/) and [Encarnación](/paraguay/place/encarnacion-and-trinidad/).** A museum of Jesuit heritage, further travel and an overnight stay in Encarnación.

On day six, the historical journey continues among the mission ruins of [Jesús](/paraguay/place/jesus/) and Trinidad. The route then heads to [Ciudad del Este](/paraguay/place/ciudad-del-este/) and, the following day, to the [Itaipu](/paraguay/place/itaipu/) hydroelectric plant.

Caapucú therefore links several historical periods without requiring a separate return to the capital. Allow enough time for travel: the museum visit and transfer to Encarnación take place on the same day.

## Who should choose a route through Caapucú?

This option suits travelers interested in history, colonial architecture and Jesuit heritage. Unlike a holiday with several nights in one city, the [8-day tour](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) changes regions: [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/), the [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/), the southern missions and [Itaipu](/paraguay/place/itaipu/). Cultural experiences sit alongside nature and the history of modern communities.

If your main objective is Casa-Oratorio Cabañas itself and an in-depth exploration of its collection, discuss the length of the stop separately when arranging the trip. The published program confirms the museum visit but does not promise an excursion of any desired duration or additional sites around Caapucú. Other journeys are listed in the [Paraguay tours catalog](/paraguay/tour/).

## What to confirm before choosing

The program includes a private transfer on the Asunción–Encarnación route, the museum visit and onward historical stops. When planning, confirm that the long transfer day is comfortable for your group, the museum is open on the selected date and the preferred guiding language is available. A Russian-speaking guide is possible by request on the 8-day journey and should therefore be agreed separately.

The product title “Paraguay 2023” reflects the historical name of the itinerary. Its page does not establish future departure dates. Choose based on the trip's content and agree on possible dates separately.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Caapucú

### How long does a visit to Caapucú take?

On the 8-day route, it is one stop on day five between Asunción and Encarnación. The exact length of the museum visit is not fixed.

### Are Caapucú and the Jesuit missions visited on the same day?

[San Ignacio Guazú](/paraguay/place/san-ignacio-guazu/) is scheduled after Caapucú on the same day, while the ruins at Trinidad and [Jesús](/paraguay/place/jesus/) are visited the following day. They are different stops featuring different historical sites.

### Do I need to book a separate hotel in Caapucú?

There is no overnight stay here on the [8-day itinerary described](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/): travelers arrive in Encarnación in the evening. See the chosen tour for accommodation conditions.

### Can I choose only the historical part of Paraguay?

You can discuss a different itinerary with Ada Tours, but a shortened program is not automatically an included option on the specified tour. For the original route, see the [Paraguay tours](/paraguay/tour/) selection.
